labs/project-chart-1.title: Define meaningful data
labs/project-chart-1.description: A fixed-scale chart for three release stages.
walkthrough: Each data entry pairs a category with a time in minutes. BarChart builds the marks, grid and labels; Scene.add makes that composite part of the rendered scene.
The orthographic camera removes perspective distortion. Its minimum vertical extent is 13; a pre updater widens that extent in a narrow canvas so the whole horizontal chart remains visible.
experiments: Set Ship to 90 and add valueSuffix: " min". Check that the axis and value labels remain legible.

labs/project-chart-2.title: Introduce the chart
labs/project-chart-2.description: Watch the bars rise in a staggered entrance.
walkthrough: Calling BarChart.animateIn first prepares the bars at their entrance state. Scene.play advances the returned Animation; awaiting it makes later instructions wait for the reveal.
The bar baselines stay fixed while their heights grow. The value labels move with the rising tops, so the labels still refer to the correct marks.
experiments: Change the entrance duration to 400, then 2400 milliseconds. Compare when the numbers become readable.

labs/project-chart-3.title: Change data through interaction
labs/project-chart-3.description: Click a bar to compare two datasets.
walkthrough: The click callback chooses the next three values, preserving category order. The busy flag guards the entire awaited transition, including rapid repeated clicks.
BarChart.animateData reuses the current scale and bar geometry. It changes value labels during interpolation, but does not replace category labels or the initial hover tooltip data.
experiments: Change the alternate values to [70, 35, 90], then click rapidly. The busy flag should keep one transition active at a time.

labs/project-diagram-1.title: Start with two nodes
labs/project-diagram-1.description: Two labeled nodes connected by a line.
walkthrough: The nodes, labels and connector are independent entities. Their initial positions come from the same node coordinates, which makes the relationship explicit in the source.

There is no follower updater in this version. Editing a node’s initial position works because initialization recalculates the endpoints; a later node.move call would need to refresh its followers too.
experiments: Edit the first node’s initial position, then add a later node.move call. Compare initialization with a change after the connector was constructed.

labs/project-diagram-2.title: Let the nodes move
labs/project-diagram-2.description: Drag either node; its label and connector follow.
walkthrough: Entity.setDraggable enables drag dispatch. The drag callback receives a world-space position, suitable for these root nodes because they have no transformed parent.
The post updater runs after other entity changes, reads both node positions and sets the line endpoints and label positions. This keeps all three drawings synchronized.
experiments: Drag both nodes and watch the labels. Temporarily remove the post updater to see which drawings stop following.

labs/project-diagram-3.title: Keep connections readable
labs/project-diagram-3.description: Drag the nodes inside the bounds and inspect the trimmed connector.
walkthrough: Clamping the received x/y coordinates keeps the nodes in the diagram’s useful area. The labels and connector derive from those clamped positions.
A normalized direction from the first center to the second supplies the two radius offsets. When the circles overlap, a center-to-center fallback avoids reversing the segment.
experiments: Drag the nodes together, then apart. Change the shared node radius and the connector inset together to preserve the boundary alignment.

labs/project-tangent-1.title: Give the curve a coordinate system
labs/project-tangent-1.description: Plot y = x² / 2 on an explicit coordinate system.
walkthrough: Axes sets the mathematical domain and the physical rectangle. FunctionGraph2D samples f and uses that coordinate system to construct the visible curve.
The shared f function will also position the moving dot and calculate the tangent in later stages. Changing that one definition keeps the mathematical objects consistent.
experiments: Replace f with Math.sin(x) + 2 and inspect the curve over the same domain.

labs/project-tangent-2.title: Animate a mathematical value
labs/project-tangent-2.description: One animated number drives a point on the curve.
walkthrough: ValueTracker starts at −2. Its Animator moves the scalar to 2 over 4500 milliseconds while a post updater reads the current value.
Axes.c2p converts (x, f(x)) to the untransformed axes rectangle. Moving the dot to that result ties its geometry to the scalar without a second animation.
experiments: Make the sweep slower, then narrow its target interval. The dot should still stay on the curve without a separate position animation.

labs/project-tangent-3.title: Reveal the changing slope
labs/project-tangent-3.description: Move the pointer after the sweep to explore the tangent.
walkthrough: The centered difference [f(x+h) − f(x−h)] / (2h) estimates slope. The line endpoints use the same f(x) and slope, then pass through Axes.c2p.
After the sweep completes, Scene.setEvent receives pointer coordinates. Axes.p2c returns [x, y]; the first element selects the tracker value, clamped to the intended domain.
experiments: Use f(x) = Math.sin(x) + 2. Compare h = 0.01 with h = 0.5, especially near a turning point.

labs/project-model-1.title: Place the models and camera
labs/project-model-1.description: A box and sphere viewed through a perspective camera.
walkthrough: The camera looks at the origin with a field of view of π/3 radians. Both models use their own materials, so color changes can be compared independently.
Sphere segment counts control the mesh silhouette. Material roughness changes surface shading; it does not add vertices or smooth the geometry.
experiments: Set widthSegments to 8 and compare the sphere outline with the original 32. Then change only its material color.

labs/project-model-2.title: Explore the scene with an orbit camera
labs/project-model-2.description: Orbit, pan and zoom around the same two models.
walkthrough: OrbitCameraController uses the camera’s initial orientation and a target at the origin. Dragging changes the viewing direction; wheel input changes the target radius.
The controller installs canvas/document input listeners and a scene updater. Scene cleanup disposes the controller; explicitly destroy it if replacing controls during a running scene.
experiments: Change radius to 6, then 15. Observe the viewing distance while the models’ positions remain fixed.

labs/project-model-3.title: Pick objects and change appearance
labs/project-model-3.description: Hover for a highlight; click to switch roughness.
walkthrough: InteractionManager raycasts the pointer against scene entities. Each model has its own hover and click callbacks, so changing one model leaves the other’s material alone.
The hover callbacks change emission strength. The click callback switches roughness between 0.8 and 0.15, then invalidates the scene so the new material is drawn.
experiments: Click each model separately. Change the glossy setting from 0.15 to 0.4 and compare its highlight.
